case_title: Mohd Muslim @ Hussain v. State (NCT of Delhi)
previous_criminal_record: No (prosecution has not shown involvement in any other case)
statutory_provisions: NDPS Act s.20, s.25, s.29; IPC s.120B
evidence_type: Recovery of ganja from co-accused; statement of co-accused who led to arrest; confessional statement of accused; bank statements of a co-accused; call records
confession: Confessional statement of the accused; prosecution relied on it, and the court only noted that reliance at the bail stage
aggravating_circumstances: Alleged recovery of 180 kg of ganja from co-accused; prosecution alleged accused was mastermind (court noted this was not backed by evidence of extensive dealing)
mitigating_circumstances: No contraband recovered from accused; no other case shown against him; age 23 at arrest; two co-accused on bail; over 7 years in custody with slow trial
high_court_outcome: Regular bail refused (order dated 08.09.2022); trial court directed to expedite trial and conclude within six months
neutral_facts: Following secret information, police conducted a raid on 28 September 2015 and allegedly found about 180 kilograms of ganja in the possession of four persons, who were arrested. During the investigation, one of the arrested persons was taken to another state to identify co-accused persons. At his instance, the accused was arrested in the early hours of 3-4 October 2015. The accused was not found in possession of any narcotic drug, and no other contraband was recovered from him. The prosecution alleged that another co-accused purchased ganja and transferred money from his bank account to the bank accounts of the accused and others before supplying the drug to a further person. Bank statements of that co-accused were relied upon to show that money had been transferred to the accused. Call records were said to show regular contact between the accused and the co-accused. The prosecution also relied on a confessional statement given by the accused. The prosecution alleged that the accused was the mastermind behind the supply of narcotic substances from another state, but no evidence of extensive dealing in narcotics was identified, and no involvement in other cases was shown. Two co-accused persons, who were not present at the raid and from whom no contraband was recovered, were the recipients of the transfers and the holders of documents relating to a seized car. One witness reportedly stated during trial that Rs. 50,000 was received from the accused. A chargesheet was filed on 29 February 2016.
number_of_offences: 4 charged (NDPS Act ss.20, 25, 29; IPC s.120B); 0 finally upheld (bail appeal, no conviction decided)
premeditation_planning: Not found by the court; the mastermind allegation was not backed by evidence
motive: alleged: payment for ganja supply through money transfers
key_evidence_accepted: No evidence was finally accepted (bail stage). The court noted reliance on the co-accused's statement, the confessional statement and bank statements, and found no further recovery from the accused
custody_duration: Over 7 years and 4 months (in custody since 03.10.2015, barring interim bail)
bail_history: Interim bail granted on several occasions (wedding ceremonies; ailing mother); regular bail refused by district court (08.06.2022) and High Court (08.09.2022); granted by Supreme Court
trial_duration: offence: 28.09.2015; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 08.09.2022; Supreme Court: 28.03.2023
legal_representation: Accused: Ms. Tanya Agarwal and Mrs. Shubhangi Tuli, Advocates. State: Vikramjit Banerjee, A.S.G., with Shreekant Neelappa Terdal and others, Advocates
investigation_status: FIR No. 148/2015; chargesheet filed 29.02.2016; supplemental chargesheets 01.08.2016 and 08.11.2017; charges framed 05.07.2016; trial ongoing (30 witnesses examined, 34 remaining)
procedural_irregularity: Delay in trial noted by the court
appeal_history: Trial court (Special Judge NDPS): bail rejected 08.06.2022. High Court: regular bail refused 08.09.2022. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, bail granted
prosecution_argument: Appellant was actively involved, implicated by call records and bank transactions with the main accused; involved in a drug network; public interest under s.37 outweighs liberty; appellant was the mastermind of supply from another state
defence_argument: Long incarceration entitles accused to bail; 34 witnesses still to be examined with little progress; parity, as the main accused and another co-accused had been granted bail
legal_principle_applied: Under s.37 NDPS, 'not guilty' is only a prima facie test; delay in trial supports bail, as s.436A CrPC applies to NDPS offences
precedent_relied_upon: Kartar Singh v. State of Punjab (1994) 3 SCC 569 (followed); Supreme Court Legal Aid Committee v. Union of India (1994) 6 SCC 731; Shaheen Welfare Association v. Union of India (1996) 2 SCC 616; Satender Kumar Antil v. CBI (2022) 10 SCC 51; Union of India v. K.A. Najeeb (2021) 3 SCC 713; Vijay Madanlal Chaudhary v. Union of India 2022 SCC OnLine SC 929 (relied on); Hussainara Khatoon (1980) 1 SCC 81; Kadra Pahadiya (1981) 3 SCC 671; Abdul Rehman Antulay (1992) 1 SCC 225; State of MP v. Kajad (2001) 7 SCC 673; Vaman Narain Ghiya (2009) 2 SCC 281 (referred to)
judicial_mitigating_factors: No recovery from accused; no other case shown; young age at arrest; co-accused on bail; prolonged custody of over 7 years with slow trial
other_sentence_order: Bail granted subject to conditions the trial court may impose; no costs
